record.paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
record.context_brief: Non-stationary case: global hyperbolicity versus self-adjointness
record.original_question: For a general non-stationary globally hyperbolic spacetime with metric of the form g = -N^2(t, x) dt^2 + g_{Σ,ij}(t, x) dxi dxj, what precise connection, if any, holds between global hyperbolicity of the Lorentzian manifold and essential self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian appearing in the Klein–Gordon equation? Equivalently, beyond the static, warped-product, and uniformly bounded sliced-space cases discussed in the paper, when does global hyperbolicity force geodesic completeness of the conformally transformed spatial slices (Σ_t, g̃_{Σ_t}), which is the ingredient used to prove essential self-adjointness?

evidence.quote: In the case of non-stationary spacetimes, however, the connection between global hyperbolicity and self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian is still unclear.
Our strategical reason for the conformal transformation is our interest in the connection of global hyperbolicity and the geodesic completeness of the Riemannian manifold (Σt, g˜Σt) for all t ∈ R.

In general however, i.e. apart from the three classes discussed above, there is no direct connection between geodesic completeness of the hypersurfaces and global hyperbolicity the Lorentzian manifold5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M, g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian manifold of dimension $n+1$ that admits a global smooth splitting $M \cong \mathbb{R} \times \Sigma$ with metric of the form
$$ g = -N^2(t,x)\, dt^2 + g_{\Sigma,ij}(t,x)\, dx^i dx^j, $$
where $N \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}\times\Sigma, (0,\infty))$ is the lapse function and, for each $t \in \mathbb{R}$, $g_{\Sigma_t} := g_{\Sigma}(t,\cdot)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on the spacelike slice $\Sigma_t := \{t\}\times\Sigma$. Assume that $(M,g)$ is globally hyperbolic, with the slices $\Sigma_t$ being smooth Cauchy hypersurfaces.

For each $t$, define the conformally rescaled spatial metric
$$ \tilde g_{\Sigma_t} := N^{-2}(t,\cdot)\, g_{\Sigma_t}, $$
and let $\tilde \Delta_t$ denote the (positive) Laplace–Beltrami operator of $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$, viewed as a symmetric operator on $C_c^\infty(\Sigma_t) \subset L^2(\Sigma_t, d\mathrm{vol}_{\tilde g_{\Sigma_t}})$.

It is known that:
(a) if each Riemannian manifold $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$ is geodesically complete, then $\tilde\Delta_t$ is essentially self-adjoint on $C_c^\infty(\Sigma_t)$;
(b) in the special cases of static spacetimes, standard warped products $g = -N^2(t)\,dt^2 + a(t)^2 h(x)$, and spacetimes with uniformly bounded lapse and uniformly equivalent slice metrics, global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ is equivalent to geodesic completeness of all $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$.

Problem. Determine the precise relationship between global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ and essential self-adjointness of the family $\{\tilde\Delta_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ on $C_c^\infty(\Sigma_t)$ for a general non-stationary metric of the form above. Equivalently, identify sharp geometric conditions on $(N, g_\Sigma)$, going beyond the three special classes (a)–(b), under which global hyperbolicity of $(M,g)$ implies geodesic completeness of $(\Sigma_t, \tilde g_{\Sigma_t})$ for every $t \in \mathbb{R}$, and conversely under which such completeness (for all $t$) implies global hyperbolicity. Either establish such an equivalence under explicit, verifiable hypotheses or construct counterexamples showing that no such implication can hold in full generality.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not reveal a definitive resolution of the general non-stationary relationship between global hyperbolicity of a Lorentzian spacetime in lapse–slicing form and essential self-adjointness of the spatial (conformally rescaled) Laplacian on Cauchy slices. Known results cover static spacetimes, warped products, and bounded-lapse settings, while the general case appears to remain unresolved in the literature.
